- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if forecast rises sharply after a spike, reduce by 10–20% for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply 3–5% downward correction for days 1–7.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (alternating +/– spikes), model overfits to recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.  
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model often underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days to compensate for lag.
